study type: Predictive Modeling Study using Cohort Data
cohort: This study utilized biomonitoring data from a population-based cohort of 788 mother-infant pairs born during 1993-1998 to mothers living near the New Bedford Harbor, to build predictive models for prenatal exposures for all 10,270 births in the same area during that period.
finding: The developed predictive models, incorporating multivariable smooths, explained a reasonable amount of variance in prenatal exposure biomarkers (R2 values ranging from 0.34 to 0.54) and can effectively predict chemical exposures for contemporaneous births in the same geographic area.
